name: Sasaki
description: Sasaki is a North Korean climbing card game for four players. Players try to get rid of all cards; temporary partnerships are determined by the two red 10s. The game is named after the combination 44A (two Fours and one Ace).

content.text: Sasaki is a North Korean climbing card game for four players. Players try to get rid of all cards; temporary partnerships are determined by the two red 10s. The game is named after the combination 44A (two Fours and one Ace).

This climbing game for four players is said to be very popular in North Korea. It is named after the special combination Sasaki (사사끼), meaning 44A (two Fours and one Ace). It is closely related to the Chinese game Red Ten (红十) but it is not clear which game is based on the other.
Four players. Temporary partnerships: the two players holding the red 10s (Heart 10 and Diamond 10) are partners; if one player holds both, that player plays alone against the other three.
48-card deck: standard international deck with all Twos and Jokers removed. Ranks from high to low: A, K, Q, J, 10, 9, 8, 7, 6, 5, 4, 3.
Standard 48-card deck (no 2s, no jokers). Score sheet (optional). Table space.
No dealer. Cards are shuffled and fanned face down; each player in turn takes the top card until all 48 are taken (12 cards each). Play is counter-clockwise.

items.text: Double sequence (ssangka): An extra ordinary combination: three or more consecutive pairs (e.g. 4-4-5-5-6-6). Beaten only by a higher double sequence of the same length or by four of a kind or Pig; not by triplet or Sasaki. Some allow double sequence to jata a single sequence of the same ranks, then a single sequence can kkota the double sequence.

Red 10s as last two cards: Some allow a player whose last two cards are the two red 10s to play them as a Pig to beat any combination and go out. Others play that a lone player with both red 10s as last two cannot play them as a pair at all, only as single cards.
